keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1971-1972, before Cliopatria's row (1973): Bahrain 'declared independence and signed a new treaty of friendship with Britain' on 15 August 1971 (Bahrain page; infobox 14 August). The shape is Cliopatria's 1973 shape plus the Hawar Islands: 'ownership' of the islands was decided 'in favour of Bahrain' by the British government in 1939 (Qatar v. Bahrain page, timeline), and Qatar's filing of 1991 sought to 'overturn the 1939 British decision to award the islands to Bahrain'. Neither Cliopatria row contains the Hawar cell.

Effective 1973-2000 (the next keyframe takes over in 2001). Cliopatria: 881.5 km2 for 1973-2023 against the infobox's 786.8 km2 (ratio 1.12; the body gives 665 km2, 'due to land reclamation, the area increased to 780 km2', no dates); the gazetteer resolves it to 2 cells (506 km2) on the main island group. Corrected by adding the Hawar Islands, in neither Bahrain's nor Qatar's Cliopatria shape: the British government decided ownership 'in favour of Bahrain' in 1939 and the Court of March 2001 kept 16 of the 17 elements with Bahrain (Qatar v. Bahrain page), so the islands are Bahrain's from independence, contested by Qatar from 1986 (ledger), not a gain of 2001.

ledger.note: April 1986: Qatar acts on Fasht al-Dibal. 'Qatar sends security force to put an end to construction work undertaken by Bahrain on then-disputed' Fasht al-Dibal (April 1986). The Hawar Islands had been in dispute since Qatar challenged the 1939 British decision that 'awards the islands to Bahrain'; Qatar filed at the ICJ in July 1991.

ledger.note: March 2001: the International Court of Justice rules. 'March 2001: Qatar v. Bahrain Maritime Delimitation and Territorial Questions (Merits) judgement is delivered' (the Hawar Islands page cites 16 March 2001).

March 2001: the Court awards Qit'at Jaradah to Bahrain. The Qatar v. Bahrain page: it 'was awarded to Bahrain on the basis of its activities there'. Counterpart nobody: the shoal was in dispute and in neither state's undisputed land, and state-of-qatar has no loss for it. The Hawar Islands are not part of this gain: the British decision of 1939 had awarded them to Bahrain and the Court kept 16 of the 17 elements with Bahrain (they are in the shape from 1971, see the keyframes), so only Janan leaves Bahrain, below. Sub-grid (a shoal), so it changes no cell.
March 2001: Bahrain loses Fasht al-Dibal. The Court awarded Qatar Zubarah 'as well as Fasht al-Dibal' (Zubarah on Qatar's mainland was never Bahraini ground).

ledger.note: 2001: Janan Island goes to Qatar. The Hawar Islands page, on the dispute 'resolved in 2001' (judgment of 16 March 2001): Janan 'was awarded to Qatar'; it is the 17th element of the group (the other page: 16 of 17 to Bahrain). The Qatar v. Bahrain page is silent on Janan.

14 February 2002: the State of Bahrain becomes the Kingdom of Bahrain. 'Changed its formal name from the State (dawla) of Bahrain to the Kingdom of Bahrain', the emir becoming king. Same state, same land.

wars.outcome: After the Fasht al-Dibal incident of April 1986 and Qatar's filing at the ICJ in July 1991, the Court's judgment of March 2001 confirmed Bahrain's title to 16 of the 17 Hawar elements (British decision of 1939) and gave it Qit'at Jaradah, and gave Qatar Zubarah, Fasht al-Dibal and Janan.
wars.note: A legal and naval dispute, not a war; the Court judged the 1939 British decision. Zubarah is excluded from the zone because it was Qatar's ground throughout.

wars.name: 2011 Bahraini uprising
wars.outcome: Protests began in early 2011; Bahrain 'requested security assistance from Saudi Arabia and other Gulf Cooperation Council countries' a month later and declared a three-month state of emergency. No territory changed.
wars.note: The page does not give the month of the request or name Peninsula Shield.

certainty.note: The Hawar Islands and Fasht al-Dibal were disputed with Qatar until the 2001 judgment; the islands' coasts were also being reclaimed (the page's 665 to 780 km2).
The ICJ judgment of March 2001 fixed the Bahrain-Qatar title; reclamation keeps adding land (the page counts 84 islands and island groups by August 2008).

notes: Written by me-10-l on 2026-10-25 from three pages (one over the 1-2 page budget: the Hawar Islands page was opened to settle Janan). SHARED WIKIDATA Q398 with bahrain (Al Madhkur, 1753-1783 in the dossier, Cliopatria 1757-1845) and, by the house-of-khalifa dossier, the House of Khalifa row: three dossiers of one island state in turn; this one starts at independence in August 1971 and is the same state as house-of-khalifa, so the colour agent may keep one hue. Cliopatria's row starts in 1973, hence the new 1971 keyframe. HAWAR (repaired 2026-10-25 after review): the Qatar v. Bahrain page dates the award of the islands to Bahrain to the British decision of 1939 ('1939: British government decides ownership in favour of Bahrain'), so they are in Bahrain's shape from independence (keyframes 1971, 1973) and the March 2001 judgment is not a gain from Qatar; Qatar never held them and its ledger has no loss. The only gain of 2001 is Qit'at Jaradah (counterpart nobody, confidence 2), and the only losses are Fasht al-Dibal and Janan, which match Qatar's two gains. Whether Bahrain held the islands in fact from 1939 to 1971 is not on the pages (the Hawar Islands page does not mention 1939). Neither Cliopatria shape contains the Hawar cell; the 2001 keyframe takes Janan out of the Hawar region, a few km2 inside what may be one grid cell. The 1986-2001 contest zone is Hawar plus Fasht al-Dibal; Zubarah, on Qatar's mainland, is not in it. The Hawar Islands page and the Qatar v. Bahrain page disagree on what is said about Janan (the first awards it to Qatar, the second is silent). PAGES SILENT: the 1986 date beyond April, the exact Hawar status before 1986, the King Fahd Causeway (1986), the Iranian claim's end (the page mentions a UN-held referendum without a date), the 2011 Peninsula Shield deployment. NAMES FOR THE GAZETTEER: Hawar Islands (region), Fasht ad Dibal, Janan Island, Qit'at Jaradah (places); the Hawar region is now also used in the keyframes, so it must resolve to land (1 cell in the gazetteer).
